documentation_revisions.previous_text: # Wave 2 analytical design · H1–H12 and one unsupervised control **Decision status.** Feature feasibility is measured. Julia approved the methods, practical effect sizes and decision rules on 15 November 2026, with the bounded control comparison recorded below. This document preserves the pre-run design. The twelve business hypotheses and the exploratory control retain their original meanings. [Research hypotheses](../../../../SEGMENTATION_HYPOTHESES_NEXT_PHASE.md) · [Learning plan](../../../../learning_plan.md) · [Executive CHECK](CHECK.md) ## Common population and measurement rules Use the corrected 17 October 2026 retrieval with the 29 September reporting cutoff. Start from 376,845 product-scope-eligible barcode–region–category assignments. Keep barcode as text. The master supplies the key, product scope, working nutrients, OFF source observations, missing flags, locked claims and ingredient evidence. The existing classification supplies membership, subtype, confidence, cereal bar flag and comparison basis. Join all three key fields exactly once. The full outer join reconciled every assignment. The shared implementation verifies the source hash and the baseline valid counts for all eight nutrients in each region and category. [Corrected master manifest](../../../01_ingestion/05_master_parquet/output/manifest.json) · [Baseline CHECK](BASELINE_CHECK.md) · [Shared diagnostic script](shared_feature_diagnostics_v1.py) **Peer** means membership YES, a named subtype, a comparable food or liquid basis and no existing cereal bar-review flag. There are 292,302 such assignments. Analyse within region × category × subtype × basis unless a row explicitly specifies pooling. Keep OTHER, unresolved membership, unresolved subtype, possible category contamination, preparation and unverified basis in the governed population and its coverage denominators. Use the existing food per 100 g and liquid per 100 ml conventions, including liquid dairy. Pack-level units are not independently verified. Preparations may contribute format and communication evidence as a separate stratum. Never convert them to ready-to-drink equivalents. Repeat supported contrasts without LOW-confidence assignments as a classification sensitivity, keeping original unrated assignments identifiable. **Valid** means the baseline working value is present, matches the OFF observation, has a clear missing flag and passes its finite governed range. Keep observed zero. There is no imputation. Energy is kcal and the seven other measurements are grams per applicable 100-unit basis. Core four means protein, total fat, total sugars and salt. All four are existing measurements. Densities, component shares, ranks, match indicators, quartile flags and ingredient cues are analytical derivations. The four numeric ratios and the ingredient cue were constructed provisionally in memory for the diagnostics. The other analytical features described below would be constructed after approval. [Raw fields, formulas and retention](FEATURE_DECISIONS.csv) **Claim comparison** means a matched, analytically eligible assessment of the exact proposition, with no source-market limitation for the regional contrasts. Compare a locked positive against documented non-detection. Keep human-confirmed negatives separate for sensitivity. Keep uncertain, unassessed, unmatched and inapplicable observations distinguishable in the source and outside that contrast. Report original core states and evidence cohort. Use the derived energy-positioning indicator and independent usable front hydration and electrolyte assessments with their own denominators. Exclude a salt-specific QA hold only when using salt. Identify historical dairy reuse and the US dairy population note in sensitivity results. Ingredient eligibility is independent of nutrition eligibility. **Evidence rules proposed for the test run.** Publish starting, measurable, assessed and retained counts by cell; report percentages with explicit denominators. Use France and UK/Ireland as primary replication opportunities, and US/Canada as selected exploratory observations. For nutritional estimates require at least 30 valid records per cell; for claim contrasts require at least 20 positives and 20 documented non-detections in the same cell before matching. Recheck sizes after matching. These are reporting floors, not power calculations. Keep smaller cells descriptive. Use barcode-level block bootstrap 95% intervals for effects and proportions, preserving repeated regional assignments. Where multiple prespecified contrasts are tested, report Benjamini–Hochberg adjusted p-values within each hypothesis alongside practical effects. Lack of support, imprecision and inadequate sample size are separate outcomes. No causal, compliance, sales or consumer-prevalence interpretation. ## Consolidated design matrix | Lens and business question | Required evidence and proposed derivation | Population and remaining diagnostics | Proposed method and output | Proposed success criterion | |---|---|---|---|---| | **1 · H1** Do formulations recur within a commercial format? | Core four. Derive within-peer high and low quartile indicators. Prespecify high protein with low sugars and high fat with high salt. Profile fibre and saturated fat where observed. | Four categories, named peers with valid core four. Check ties, zero IQR and replication across regions within the same subtype. | Descriptive formulation profiles and a within-cell permutation of one constituent for each association. Compare observed joint frequency with the independence expectation. Report constituents in grams. | At least one profile exceeds expectation by 5 percentage points in two primary-region cells of the same format, with adjusted evidence at 0.05. Tied boundaries that cannot distinguish high and low are uninformative. | | **1 · H2** How often does similar energy hide a material sugars difference? | Energy and total sugars. Derive absolute within-pair differences. Optional sugars/carbohydrate share only on its own valid subset. | Primary comparison granola and flakes separately within each region, valid energy and sugars, 4,230 assignments. Check final pair coverage, energy overlap, LOW confidence and ties. | Sort by energy then text GTIN, pair adjacent unused products from lowest energy upward when within 10 kcal/100 g, otherwise advance one. No reuse or self-match. Report median sugar gap and fraction ≥5 g/100 g. Repeat at 5 and 20 kcal and with reverse-direction pairing. | In the same subtype in FR and UK/IE, at least 25% of pairs differ by ≥5 g sugars, with lower 95% bound above 15% and consistent direction across matching sensitivities. Other categories remain context. | | **2 · H3** Does changing the denominator reorder products? | Protein or fibre, separately, plus energy. Compare observed concentration to 100 × nutrient / energy on identical rows. Derive within-cell percentile ranks with average ties. | Named peers with the individual nutrient and energy ≥10. Repeat for energy >0, ≥5 and ≥20. Report tied zeros and rankable sample size. | Paired rank comparison by format and region. Show Spearman correlation and proportion moving ≥25 percentile points. Keep solids and liquids separate. | At least 15% move ≥25 points for one nutrient in a format replicated in both primary regions; show interval and threshold sensitivity. Do not infer fibre results from protein completeness. | | **2 · H4** Can high concentration coincide with high energy and a weaker per-calorie position? | Same individual nutrient and energy as H3. Derive concentration, energy and density quartiles on identical rows. | Same H3 population per nutrient and denominator sensitivity. Check ties, nonzero group sizes and extreme density ratios. | Paired cross-tab. Among upper-quartile concentration products, count those also in the upper energy quartile but at/below median density. Separately show lower-half concentration and upper-quartile density. | Primary trade-off occurs in ≥10% of the upper-concentration group with ≥30 such group members, replicated in the same format in FR and UK/IE. Report both directions separately. | | **3 · H5** Does a nutrient proposition distinguish products on the corresponding measurement? | Locked protein, fibre, reduced-sugar, sugar-free or reduced-fat proposition plus its own measured protein, fibre, total sugars or total fat. Optional per-calorie sensitivity requires energy. | Claim comparison within the same peer cell. Check each proposition's arm size, subtype mix and source cohort. Reduced sugar and sugar-free stay separate. | Observational difference in medians between assessed arms, with uncertainty; compare named formats where enough arms exist. | Prespecified directional separation ≥2 g for protein, fibre or fat, or ≥3 g total sugars per applicable 100 units, with interval excluding zero. Report which tests clear the floor; interpret relative reduction language as communication only. | | **3 · H6** Do similar formulations tell different pack stories? | Core four, plus separately assessed protein, organic, plant-based, gluten-free, natural and heritage propositions. Derive nutrition-only proximity; keep the claims out of matching. | Within a single peer cell and proposition-assessed subset. Test achievable one-to-one caliper match counts and zero-IQR dimensions; inspect actual nutrient gaps. | Pair distinct products on nearest robust-scaled nutrition, maximum 0.25 reference IQR on each dimension; require equality on zero-IQR dimensions. Stable GTIN tie-break, no reuse. Report claim discordance and matched coverage per proposition. | At least 30 pairs in a cell and ≥20% discordant, lower 95% bound >10%. Report sparse territories descriptively. The pre-match arm counts are screening diagnostics only. | | **3 · H7** Can similar declared ingredients accompany different propositions? | Eligible ingredients_text, ingredients_lang and locked protein/plant-based/no-artificial states. Start with an explicit EN/FR pea- or soy-protein phrase. Cue missing for unusable text. | Named peers with usable non-placeholder FR/EN/BOTH ingredient text and assessment of the exact claim. Check ingredient wording, negation, synonyms, precautionary statements and language sensitivity. | Start with protein communication. Cross-tab cue detected versus no matching phrase within each assessed arm. Show actual phrase and audited error rates. Expand cue families only after validation. | Require ≥90% precision on reviewed hits and ≥80% recall against a stratified hand-labelled validation sample including non-hits. Then require ≥10 pp difference between assessed arms with interval excluding zero, or document overlap descriptively when support is insufficient. | | **3 · H8** Do energy and hydration/electrolyte beverages communicate distinct roles at comparable composition? | Locked energy_positioning and its basis/format, usable hydration and electrolyte front statuses independently, energy and sugars for nutritional comparisons. | RTD named liquid beverage peers; require joint observability for overlap estimates and valid nutrition for composition. Separately describe registry-identified preparations. Report all incomplete panel counts. | Proposition-specific cohort profiles and 2×2 tables on jointly assessed products. Marginal counts from different extraction layers cannot estimate overlap. | A comparative contrast would require ≥20 in each distinct territory arm in a common format. Present wave supports descriptive counts only. A sparse or empty intersection cannot establish that the territories are mutually exclusive. | | **4 · H9** Does positive positioning coexist with a less-visible trade-off? | Protein claim × salt, fibre claim × total sugars, reduced-fat claim × total sugars. Derive upper-quartile attribute indicator from all valid nutritional peers, independently of claim sampling. | Exact proposition and single trade-off attribute per contrast. Apply salt-specific QA. Check peer threshold, zero inflation and assessed arms. | Calculate coexistence counts and peer-adjusted percentage-point difference between positive and documented non-detection arms. No composite score. | Identify a material coexistence pattern if ≥25% of positives exceed peer Q3 and the rate exceeds the comparison arm by ≥10 pp with interval excluding zero. Report coexistence even if there is no between-arm distinction. | | **4 · H10** Does the same trade-off differ between positioning territories? | Locked organic, plant-based and protein propositions plus sugars. Use the same peer-defined high-sugars indicator as H9; preserve multiple positive flags. | Restrict to common peer cells and products with both compared territories assessable. Check overlapping positives, exclusive-arm sizes and common threshold. | Compare organic-only and protein-only first. Report dual positives and neither separately. Add plant-based only with common support. Standardize across shared cells using equal cell weights. | ≥20 in each exclusive arm per retained cell, ≥10 pp difference in upper-quartile sugars with interval excluding zero. A pooled difference driven solely by category mix is insufficient. | | **4 · H11** How often is a measurable nutrient advantage undetected on assessed packs? | Protein or fibre density with its corresponding exact claim. Derive advantage as strictly above peer Q3 based on valid composition before intersecting assessed evidence. | Same H3 primary density gate. Require ≥30 measurable reference products and known same-proposition status. Report uncertain and unmatched counts separately; check ties at Q3 and the source cohort. | Among high-density assessed products, report documented non-detection fraction and interval. List human-confirmed negatives separately. Compare both nutrients individually. | ≥30 informative high-density assessments in a peer cell and lower 95% bound for documented non-detection above 10%. Describe potential undercommunication on the assessed evidence only. | | **Cross-lens · H12** Do the same formulations recur across geographies with different observed frequencies or communication? | Text GTIN, region, category, subtype and basis, plus exactly the H1 profile features or one H5 proposition and matched nutrient. Reuse H1/H5 derivations. | Common subtype and basis with adequate per-region support. Apply FR reference cut points unchanged to comparators for frequency comparisons. Examine GTIN overlap, regional coverage and sensitivity to shared barcodes. | Show cell-specific differences and direct standardization with equal shared-cell weights. Separate observed-assortment composition from selected pack assessments. Compare FR and UK/IE primarily; show conditional US/CA estimates only. | Report a geographic difference if ≥10 pp with interval excluding zero and direction stable to excluding shared GTINs and reweighting. If common support fails, restrict to a named contrast or report counts. No US segment prevalence estimate. | | **5 · One unsupervised control** What structure emerges without using business hypotheses or claims? | Core four only. Map each to its empirical percentile in the FR/UK reference using midranks for ties. Preserve unscaled original grams for interpretation. | One row per distinct GTIN in named, comparable **solid** foods from FR and UK/IE; deterministic first sort by barcode, region, category. Require all four valid. Hold US foods for exploratory assignment and flag previously seen GTINs. | One k-means control on the four percentiles, initial reference k=4. Compare k=3–5 on identical inputs, seed 42, 20 initializations, bootstrap samples and evaluation records. Expand only for a documented reason. Select k on stability, interpretability and analytical usefulness. Compute stability under product bootstrap using the same specification. Profile original measurements, format, category, region and assessed claims after fitting. | Propose median adjusted Rand index ≥0.70 across resamples, silhouette ≥0.25 and each group ≥5%. Report adjusted mutual information with format; if ≥0.50 or groups mainly reproduce obvious categories, describe a format-dominated control. Weak stability is a valid result. | ## Feature and implementation decisions - **Protein claim provenance.** Of 385 H5 protein positives with comparable measured protein, 191 have direct OCR wording, 169 a saved model assessment, 24 an approved existing rule and one a historical saved assessment. Compare the primary estimate with a direct-wording estimate. Report rule-supported positives separately because an existing numeric protein implication can contribute to the classification. The locked proposition records communicated positioning; the nutritional outcome comes from the separate OFF measurement. - **Shared nutrition basis.** Retain total fat and sugars in the core matrix. Saturated fat remains a meaningful absolute measure for targeted profiling. Total carbohydrates supplies the context for sugars. Adding both parents and components to a distance would give some nutritional axes extra weight. The pooled food reference gives fat/saturated-fat Pearson 0.871 and Spearman 0.845, and carbohydrates/sugars 0.736 and 0.762. Relationships differ by format. Interpret correlations on their printed paired counts. Energy is a matching or denominator variable where the question requires it. The all-eight matrix has energy VIF 118, fat 99 and carbohydrates 67. The four core VIFs range from 1.09 to 1.44. [Pair counts and both correlation matrices](FEATURE_CORRELATIONS.csv) - **Ratios.** Missing numerator, missing denominator and observed zero denominator yield undefined ratios. A measured zero numerator with a valid positive denominator yields zero. Keep primary density rankings at ≥10 kcal per 100 units and show alternatives. Review tail leverage and rank displacement before interpreting an extreme. Use component shares as secondary descriptors only; flag values above one and parent amounts below 1 g, report sensitivities restricted to coherent pairs and parents ≥1 g. Do not cap, repair or delete the source. Ratio extremes can reflect rounding, small denominators or discordant inputs; diagnostics cannot identify the cause for an individual product. - **Scaling and ties.** Report nutritional contrasts in original units. Use peer ranks for H3/H4 and within-cell quartiles for specific comparisons. For high/low H1 use strict above Q3/below Q1; flag cells where either indicator is empty. For H4 report tie counts and use inclusive concentration and energy quartiles only when boundaries distinguish groups. A strict H9/H10 threshold excludes ties exactly at Q3. Reserve robust IQR calipers for H6 and reference-percentile scaling for the one control. Percentiles bound numerical leverage but discard absolute distance, so report original-unit medians/IQRs and tails for every control group. No global log transform, outlier filter, normalization or imputation. - **Execution and interpretation.** Group resamples by barcode and preserve the analysis unit in uncertainty estimates; for H2/H6 resample whole matched pairs within a cell. For H12 use a shared-barcode sensitivity in addition to block resampling. Recalculate study-specific peer thresholds within resamples when population-estimated. Lock pairing tolerances, tails, reporting floors and practical thresholds together before the run. The thresholds are commercial research conventions proposed for this wave; they are not dietary limits or independently validated materiality cutoffs. - **Deferred inputs.** Use NOVA only in an explicitly processing-related comparison with its own availability denominator. Defer rules for new ingredient families, inferred added sugar, claims outside the locked taxonomy and ingredient-list interpretations of certification. Sampling-group labels, outcomes, brand/company and OCR metadata stay outside the control distance; they may describe groups when appropriate. A recurring H1 product profile need not coincide with a control cluster. ## Reproduction and scope of the diagnostics Run the repository virtual-environment Python on `shared_feature_diagnostics_v1.py` from any working directory. It reads the corrected master and the three existing baseline CSVs. It outputs the inventory and upper-triangular Pearson/Spearman tables in this directory. Correlations pool regions only within the stated category and basis, except for the explicitly labelled distinct FR/UK solid-food reference. They describe redundancy and have no between-region inferential interpretation. VIF uses a common complete-case matrix for each specified feature set. Self-correlations give univariate counts; off-diagonals use pairwise complete observations. The named-peer diagnostics count assignments unless explicitly labelled distinct GTIN. Filter the inventory by `record_kind`. `raw` separates source availability from valid observations. `joint` and `peer_retention` give set-specific denominators. `engineered` and `energy_sensitivity` describe provisional ratios. `H2_energy_only` counts candidate neighbours before matching. For `claim_comparison`, retained_n means composition/text/peer eligible from the locked layer **before** restricting to known claim states; sum the positive and documented-negative columns for the primary contrast. `cells_20_each` counts peer cells meeting the prespecified two-arm screening floor. `claim_feature` preserves the original core state counts. `H7_text_support` counts literal text hits within assessed arms. `H8_joint` measures joint evidence with nutrition. `H12_common_support` counts comparable subtype–basis cells, not products. The five lens folders link to the relevant decision rows and share this implementation.

"""Rebuild only juice-dependent analytical artifacts; stop before consolidation.

One validated shared master read is reused by the existing builders. Original
labels are reproducible via beverages_v1.refine_original, not a duplicate dataset.
"""
from pathlib import Path
import ast
import hashlib
import importlib.util
import json
import re
import sys

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import pyarrow.parquet as pq

HERE=Path(__file__).resolve().parent
LENSES=HERE.parent
L3=LENSES/"03_claims_composition_and_ingredients"
L4=LENSES/"04_positioning_tradeoffs"
STUDY=LENSES.parent
EDA=STUDY/"02_shared_preprocessing_and_eda/02_eda/00_shared_baseline_and_feature_diagnostics"
sys.path[:0]=[str(HERE),str(EDA)]
from shared_feature_diagnostics_v1 import KEY,MASTER,read_master
from juice_classification_v1 import VERSION,regression_checks,NAMED


def digest(path):
    with path.open("rb") as f:return hashlib.file_digest(f,"sha256").hexdigest()


def load(path):
    spec=importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(path.stem,path)
    m=importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec);spec.loader.exec_module(m)
    return m


def table(head,rows):
    return "\n".join("| "+" | ".join(str(v).replace("|","/") for v in row)+" |" for row in [head,["---"]*len(head),*rows])


def equivalent(left,right,keys,drop=()):
    left=left.drop(columns=list(drop),errors="ignore").sort_values(keys).reset_index(drop=True)
    right=right.drop(columns=list(drop),errors="ignore").sort_values(keys).reset_index(drop=True)
    pd.testing.assert_frame_equal(left,right,check_dtype=False,check_exact=False,rtol=1e-12,atol=1e-12)


def affected_coverage(x):
    return x.cohort_family.eq("juice detail") | (x.cohort_family.eq("accepted") &
        x.branch.isin(["beverages/"+s for s in NAMED|{"juice family unresolved"}]))


def update_notes(coverage,beverage,juice):
    path=L3/"communication_coverage_CHECK_v1.md"

# Tuesday communication coverage CHECK · 17 November 2026

**PROCEED with a reduced positioning scope.** The accepted formulation profiles reproduce correctly, but pack-evidence coverage differs sharply between them. Granola supports descriptive communication overlays in both primary regions. UK/Irish soda supports a specific sugar-free comparison. Cream/pudding, lower-fat potato crisps and the energy-drink formulation split have insufficient primary-region evidence for comparable claim contrasts.

## Delivery scope and documentation

The [segmentation methodology](../../../SEGMENTATION.md) establishes the accepted hierarchy, feature-specific eligibility, current analytical code locations and the Lovable analytical package due Saturday 21 November. The completed k=5 control remains contextual evidence. The dated learning plan allocates communication work to Wednesday, bounded NOVA/boundary work to Thursday, package consolidation to Friday, and acceptance/corrections to Saturday. Julia starts layout work Sunday 22 November. Historical RUNs and original hypotheses remain provenance.

## Evidence available on the five retained profiles

Each entry below gives **positive / documented non-detection**, with known count divided by the full nutritional-profile population. Unknown and unassessed records are outside the known denominator.

| Retained nutritional profile | Exact proposition | France | UK/Ireland | Decision |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Granola | Fibre | 8 / 17; 25/251 known (10.0%) | 16 / 9; 25/94 known (26.6%) | Descriptive overlay in both regions. |
| Granola | Protein | 0 / 25; 25/251 known | 7 / 19; 26/94 known | UK/IE exploratory; French zeros concern assessed evidence only. |
| Cream/pudding | Protein | 0 / 0; 0/27 known | 1 / 0; 1/15 known | No supported comparison. |
| Lower-fat potato crisps | Reduced fat | 0 / 0; 0/100 known | 3 / 0; 3/90 known | No supported comparison. |
| Very-low-sugars soda | Sugar-free | 6 / 1; 7/713 known (1.0%) | 28 / 15; 43/255 known (16.9%) | UK/IE supported for comparison; France descriptive only. |
| Very-low-sugars energy drinks | Sugar-free | 1 / 1; 2/153 known (1.3%) | 6 / 3; 9/88 known (10.2%) | Too sparse for a formulation contrast. |

Matched, eligible assessments themselves number 35 FR/30 UK/IE in the granola profile, 0/1 in cream/pudding, 0/6 in potato crisps, 13/59 in soda, and 3/11 in energy drinks. An assessment match does not make every proposition known. In UK/Irish potato crisps, six matches supply three known reduced-fat propositions. Missing nutrition was not imputed to gain evidence coverage.

## Proposed Wednesday scope

1. **Granola communication within the accepted hierarchy.** Show protein, fibre and organic on the retained profile versus other measurable granola. For fibre, the comparison groups contain 24 positives and 78 documented non-detections in France, and 48/26 in UK/IE. The profile arms themselves each have 25 known assessments. Use counts, effect sizes and uncertainty; treat regional agreement as exploratory given the small selected arms. The UK/Irish protein comparison is 7/26 known profile assessments versus 3/74 in other measurable granola. Avoid interpreting this as population prevalence.
2. **UK/Irish soda, measured sugars and sugar-free communication.** In the retained profile, 28/43 known assessments are positive; in other measurable sodas, 1/43 is positive and 42 have documented non-detection. This provides a supported exact-proposition comparison. “Other measurable” includes intermediate sugars; keep measured amounts visible. Use the existing H5 soda result as related evidence.
3. **Reuse supported commercial-format findings.** At the full commercial level, fibre has at least 20 positives and 20 documented non-detections in granola and flakes in both primary regions. French granola organic and UK/Irish granola plant-based also pass that same-proposition screening floor. Reuse completed findings before adding a test. The screening flag is a sample-size check, with additional nutrient availability required for a composition contrast.
4. **Record evidence gaps explicitly.** Keep the measured cream/pudding and potato profiles even though their communication evidence is sparse. Present energy-positioning counts and beverage functional evidence descriptively. H8 remains descriptive. Source-market limitations, human exceptions and claim provenance need their existing treatment during interpretation.

None of the five profile arms supports a within-arm positive-versus-documented-non-detection contrast at the earlier 20-in-each-state floor in FR or UK/IE. This differs from comparing proposition rates across two formulation arms: UK/Irish soda has 43 known records in each formulation arm. Small granola arms can supply descriptive overlays with uncertainty. These criteria answer different questions.

## Reading the coverage table

The [consolidated table](communication_coverage_v1.csv) has **13,602 proposition-specific cells**, covering **121 labelled cohort families/branches** across three regions. It evaluates all 33 locked core propositions except the source energy-claim flag, plus the approved derived energy positioning and independent hydration/electrolyte propositions for beverages. It retains the locked taxonomy and makes no new claim assessments.

- `baseline` cohorts supply named-subtype context, including branches without a completed within-format follow-up. They do not establish new approved profiles.
- `accepted` cohorts use the follow-up hierarchy, including explicitly unresolved and scope-caution branches. `juice detail` refines the existing juice cohort. The cohort-family label denotes which existing classification is reused; it does not verify every product's identity.
- `commercial population` is the starting branch. The five profile branches are also partitioned into retained profile, other measurable and required-measurement-unknown slices. The latter includes records failing the approved energy floor for cream/pudding. Empty slices have no row.
- Coverage uses the original barcode–region–category assignment unit. Parent/child, baseline/refined and profile/comparison rows overlap. Do not sum these rows to produce a unique-product or claim-evidence total.
- The primary known denominator is positive plus documented non-detection for the specific proposition. Human-confirmed negatives remain separate. Uncertain, other unknown assessed, unassessed and market-limited states remain distinct and reconcile to the population.
- Exact source-market limitations exclude a record from primary regional claim comparisons while retaining it in the population and its own count. Historical reuse and the US dairy population QA note have separate count columns for later sensitivity. No source QA note is treated as human verification.
- Preparations have communication coverage in their separate commercial population; this supplies no approval for nutritional comparison on an unverified basis. Explicit alcohol branches are omitted. Remaining unresolved identities retain uncertainty.

## Validation and audit

The [versioned coverage pass](communication_coverage_v1.py) reuses the shared corrected-master reader and approved cereal/dairy classifiers and snack/beverage/juice keys. It verifies the Wave 2 digest, original regional nutrient-valid totals, one-to-one joins, all 15 accepted regional profile counts, cell uniqueness and complete state reconciliation. All core and derived proposition fields are read from locked evidence. Profile rules are applied without requiring unrelated nutrients. The source and historical outputs remain unchanged.

This pass measures feasibility and coverage. It runs no hypothesis tests, extraction or additional clustering. US/Canada remains a selected exploratory population. Communicated protein positives can include approved existing rules; subsequent interpretation should use the stored basis to distinguish direct wording from rule-supported evidence.

**Tuesday scope complete.** The material finding is the mismatch between the broad nutritional population and the smaller assessed-communication population. Wednesday can produce useful, bounded findings while retaining explicit evidence gaps.

"""Bounded control comparison; invoke from the project environment."""
import sys
from pathlib import Path
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans
from sklearn.metrics import adjusted_mutual_info_score, adjusted_rand_score, silhouette_score
from threadpoolctl import threadpool_limits

ROOT=Path(__file__).resolve().parent
sys.path.insert(0,str(ROOT.parent/"02_shared_preprocessing_and_eda/02_eda/00_shared_baseline_and_feature_diagnostics"))
from shared_feature_diagnostics_v1 import read_master, CORE, KEY

OUT=ROOT/"05_unsupervised_control"

def ecdf(frame, reference):
    result=[]
    for name in CORE:
        values=np.sort(reference[name].to_numpy())
        x=frame[name].to_numpy()
        result.append((np.searchsorted(values,x,"left")+np.searchsorted(values,x,"right"))/(2*len(values)))
    return np.column_stack(result)

def fit(x,k):
    return KMeans(n_clusters=k,n_init=20,random_state=42,algorithm="lloyd").fit(x)

def main():
    source,_=read_master()
    foods=source[source.peer & source.basis_group.eq("per_100g_food")]
    ref=foods[foods.region.isin(["FR","UK-IE"])].sort_values(KEY).drop_duplicates("barcode").dropna(subset=CORE)
    us=foods[foods.region.eq("US-CA")].sort_values(KEY).dropna(subset=CORE).drop_duplicates("barcode")
    assert len(ref)==114146 and len(us)==13911
    x=ecdf(ref,ref); xu=ecdf(us,ref)
    evaluation=np.random.default_rng(42).choice(len(ref),4000,replace=False)
    all_rows=pd.concat([ref,us],ignore_index=True)
    assignments=all_rows[KEY+["subtype"]].copy()
    assignments["population"]=["reference"]*len(ref)+list(np.where(us.barcode.isin(ref.barcode),"US seen","US unseen"))
    assert assignments.population.eq("US unseen").sum()==12036
    rows=[]
    for k in [4,3,5]:
        model=fit(x,k)
        labels=model.labels_
        stability=[]
        for seed in range(12):
            sample=np.random.default_rng(2000+seed).integers(0,len(x),len(x))
            test=fit(x[sample],k)
            stability.append(adjusted_rand_score(labels,test.predict(x)))
        sil=silhouette_score(x[evaluation],labels[evaluation])
        names=np.argsort(np.argsort(model.cluster_centers_[:,2]))+1
        lab=names[np.r_[labels,model.predict(xu)]]
        assignments[f"k{k}"]=lab
        mix=adjusted_mutual_info_score(ref.subtype,labels)
        rows.append(dict(kind="evaluation",k=k,n=len(x),ari_median=np.median(stability),
                         ari_min=min(stability),ari_max=max(stability),silhouette=sil,format_ami=mix,
                         min_share=np.bincount(labels).min()/len(labels),inertia=model.inertia_))
        for (pop,group),g in all_rows.assign(population=assignments.population,group=lab).groupby(["population","group"]):
            row=dict(kind="profile",k=k,population=pop,group=group,n=len(g),top_format=g.subtype.mode()[0],
                     top_format_share=g.subtype.value_counts(normalize=True).iloc[0])
            for m in CORE:
                row[m]=g[m].median()
                row[m+"_q1"],row[m+"_q3"]=g[m].quantile([.25,.75])
            rows.append(row)
            for col in ["category","region","subtype"]:
                for val,n in g[col].value_counts().items():
                    rows.append(dict(kind="profile_mix",population=pop,k=k,group=group,variable=col,value=val,n=n,denominator=len(g)))
            for c in ["protein_claim","organic_claim","plant_based_claim","fibre_claim"]:
                a=g[g.assessed_layer & g.claims_source_market_limitation.fillna("").eq("")]
                positive=a["claims_claim_"+c].eq(True).sum()
                negative=a["claims_state_"+c].eq("DOCUMENTED_NOT_DETECTED").sum()
                rows.append(dict(kind="claim_profile",population=pop,k=k,group=group,variable=c,n=positive,
                                 denominator=positive+negative,assessed_layer_n=len(a),group_n=len(g)))
        print("control",k,sil,np.median(stability),flush=True)
    pd.DataFrame(rows).to_csv(OUT/"control_comparison_v1.csv",index=False)
    assignments.to_parquet(OUT/"control_assignments_v1.parquet",index=False)

if __name__=="__main__":
    with threadpool_limits(limits=2):
        main()
